report.incidentSummary: Assistant replies taking 20+ seconds: Since about 11:20 IST assistant replies take 20 seconds or more and some conversations end with 'Something went wrong'. We also kicked off a knowledge index rebuild at 11:00 IST today.
report.rootCauseStatement: Not determined. This report was generated by code from the evidence ledger because the reporting agent failed (aborted).

hypotheses.cause: assistant-orchestrator exceeded the llm-provider rate limit of 200,000 tokens per minute, triggering HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses and multiple backoff retries (2-8 seconds each) that inflated conversation latency to 20+ seconds and caused generic fallback errors when retries were exhausted.
hypotheses.rationale: Directly supported by orchestrator metrics and logs showing a simultaneous surge in rate_limited_count (from ~0 to 79/min), retry_count (from ~1 to 65/min), and llm_latency_p95_ms (from ~5s to >22s) starting at 05:50 UTC. Error logs explicitly document '429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000)' and fallback messages upon 3 retry exhaustion.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream llm-provider experienced an unannounced quota recalculation or throttling degradation at 05:50 UTC, enforcing a 200,000 tokens per minute cap on assistant-orchestrator despite prior traffic running at 210,000-267,000 tokens per minute without throttling.
hypotheses.rationale: assistant-orchestrator was running at 210,000 to 267,000 tokens/min between 05:00 and 05:45 UTC without any 429 errors or elevated retries. At 05:50 UTC, 429 errors abruptly began with 'limit=200000', suggesting the upstream provider may have newly applied or throttled to this lower limit.

confidence.rationale: No agent-written report; hypotheses (if any) are listed as unresolved.

candidates.cause: Upstream LLM provider latency degradation or queuing causing assistant queries to take over 20 seconds and occasionally time out
candidates.whyPlausible: assistant-orchestrator calls llm-provider with a 25000ms timeout and 2 retries. Slowness or queuing at the hosted LLM provider directly matches the 20-30s response time and occasional failures hitting the api-gateway 30000ms timeout.

findings.summary: A full index rebuild on knowledge-index (CHG-48222) was initiated at 05:30 UTC (11:00 IST), approximately 20 minutes before symptom onset (~05:50 UTC). No other deployments or config changes occurred on assistant-orchestrator or indexing-pipeline in the investigation window. A similar past incident (PIR-2003) previously caused 8-10s assistant delays during an index rebuild; however, assistant-orchestrator enforces an 800ms timeout on knowledge-index queries, suggesting that 20+ second delays likely involve downstream llm-provider latency (25s timeout) or combined upstream/downstream effects.

observations.statement: At 2026-10-07T05:30:00.000Z (11:00 IST), infrastructure change CHG-48222 was executed by p.nair on knowledge-index: 'full index rebuild started (embedding model refresh)' (build 4121).
No deployments or configuration changes were executed for assistant-orchestrator or indexing-pipeline during the window 2026-10-07T04:30:00.000Z to 2026-10-07T07:30:00.000Z.

Earlier deployments and config changes on 2026-10-06 included CHG-48496 on assistant-orchestrator (v0.42.0 to v0.42.1 at 12:26 UTC) and CHG-48506 on indexing-pipeline (autoscaling max_replicas raised to 16 at 17:14 UTC), both occurring over 12 hours before the incident onset.

Past incident PIR-2003 (2026-09-02) previously involved assistant slowness during a knowledge index rebuild (search p95 rose to 2.5s and assistant answers took 8-10s), which was resolved by running rebuilds on separate nodes.
assistant-orchestrator calls knowledge-index synchronously with an 800ms timeout (0 retries) and calls llm-provider with a 25000ms timeout (2 retries).

While CHG-48222 (full index rebuild) coincided closely with the onset (~20 minutes prior), the 800ms timeout from assistant-orchestrator to knowledge-index cannot alone account for 20+ second response times unless llm-provider or other downstream calls are also experiencing elevated latency or retries.

findings.summary: assistant-orchestrator experienced elevated llm_latency_p95_ms (jumping from ~5s to >22s), sharply increased rate_limited_count (from ~0 to 60-79/min), and increased retry_count (from ~1 to 50-65/min) starting exactly at 05:50 UTC. Logs confirm upstream llm-provider returned HTTP 429 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000'. The high latency and user-facing failures were driven by backoff retries on 429 quota throttling rather than provider timeouts.

observations.statement: assistant-orchestrator's llm_latency_p95_ms rose sharply starting at 05:50 UTC (from baseline ~5,000-5,400 ms up to 11,252 ms at 05:50 UTC, and then 22,000-23,347 ms from 05:55 UTC onward).
assistant-orchestrator's rate_limited_count jumped from baseline ~0/min to 33.38/min at 05:50 UTC, and stayed elevated between 55 and 79/min through the rest of the window.
assistant-orchestrator's retry_count jumped from baseline 0.4-1.2/min to 26.47/min at 05:50 UTC, and remained elevated between ~49 and 66/min through 07:30 UTC.

Logs show that beginning at 2026-10-07T05:50:04.497Z, assistant-orchestrator received HTTP 429 errors from llm-provider stating 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000', triggering retries with backoff intervals of 2-8 seconds.

When 3 retries were exhausted on 429 errors, assistant-orchestrator logged conversation failures ('llm-provider 429 after 3 attempts; returned fallback message') and served fallback error responses to users.
The elevated llm_latency_p95_ms (20+ seconds) was caused by repeated 429 rate limit backoff retries to llm-provider rather than upstream slow model generation or network timeouts.
Token consumption before 05:50 UTC was 210,000-267,000 tokens/min; at 05:50 UTC enforcement or reduction of the 200,000 tokens/min limit began triggering 429 rate limiting.

findings.summary: Following the 05:30 UTC (11:00 IST) index rebuild, knowledge-index showed a mild latency rise (p95 increased from ~85ms to ~350-370ms, recovering by 07:15 UTC) due to cold cache warming (build 4121 warming while build 4120 served). Neither knowledge-index nor indexing-pipeline exhibited elevated error rates, queue lag, lock contention, or 20+ second latency spikes. The rebuild and knowledge-index can be ruled out as the primary cause of the 20+ second assistant delays.

observations.statement: knowledge-index latency_p95_ms rose from ~85-91ms (pre-05:30 UTC) to ~330-369ms between 05:35 and 07:05 UTC, returning to baseline (~85ms) by 07:15 UTC.
knowledge-index error_rate remained steady at ~0.08% to 0.12% across the entire investigation window without any elevation.
indexing-pipeline queue_lag_s remained stable between 22.8s and 35.2s, and ingest_errors stayed negligible (0 to 0.2/min, mean 0.04/min).

knowledge-index and indexing-pipeline had zero ERROR or FATAL logs; knowledge-index WARN logs showed build 4120 serving while build 4121 warmed with cold cache on 21-45% of queries and occasional slow searches of 400-666ms.

The 05:30 UTC rebuild caused a slight increase in knowledge-index p95 latency (up to ~370ms) due to cold cache during index warming, but neither knowledge-index nor indexing-pipeline showed 20+ second delays, elevated errors, queue lag, or lock contention. They are not the root cause of the incident.

## Summary
Assistant replies taking 20+ seconds: Since about 11:20 IST assistant replies take 20 seconds or more and some conversations end with 'Something went wrong'. We also kicked off a knowledge index rebuild at 11:00 IST today.

**Root cause:** Not determined. This report was generated by code from the evidence ledger because the reporting agent failed (aborted).

Error logs explicitly document '429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000)' and fallback messages upon 3 retry exhaustion.
2. **Upstream llm-provider experienced an unannounced quota recalculation or throttling degradation at 05:50 UTC, enforcing a 200,000 tokens per minute cap on assistant-orchestrator despite prior traffic running at 210,000-267,000 tokens per minute without throttling.** — `llm-provider`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.35, unresolved
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_9, ev_13, ev_16] · Contradicting: none
